## Installing birdnetR

Install the released version from CRAN:

```r
install.packages("birdnetR")
```

or the development version from GitHub:

```r
pak::pak("birdnet-team/birdnetR")
```


## How Python is set up

You don't need to install Python yourself. birdnetR uses
[`reticulate::py_require()`](https://rstudio.github.io/reticulate/reference/py_require.html):
the first time you use birdnetR, reticulate downloads Python and the `birdnet`
Python package with [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) and keeps them in a cache.
The first setup takes a few minutes; later sessions reuse the cache and start
within seconds.

The default setup contains ONNX Runtime and LiteRT. It runs BirdNET+ V3.0 and
BirdNET V2.4, and custom TFLite classifiers trained on V2.4.

`birdnet_sitrep()` shows which Python and which `birdnet` version birdnetR
uses (see [Troubleshoot](Troubleshoot.html#reporting-a-problem)).


## Extra downloads

Some models need TensorFlow or PyTorch on top of the default setup:

| You load | birdnetR installs | Download |
|---|---|---|
| `birdnet_load_perch()` | TensorFlow | about 600 MB |
| `birdnet_load(backend = "pb")`, Raven exports | TensorFlow | about 600 MB |
| `backend = "tf"` with `library = "tflite"`, or where LiteRT is not available (Intel Macs, Windows on ARM) | TensorFlow | about 600 MB |
| `birdnet_load(backend = "pt")` | PyTorch | several GB with GPU support (about 6 GB for AMD GPUs), much less for the CPU-only version |

birdnetR installs these the first time you load such a model, even in the
middle of an R session. That first load takes longer. The `needs` column of
`birdnet_list_models()` shows which model needs what (see
[Models and backends](models.html)).

On Linux, uv installs the CUDA build of PyTorch by default, which is several GB
even if you have no GPU. To get the CPU-only build, run
`Sys.setenv(UV_TORCH_BACKEND = "cpu")` before the first birdnetR call.

### Download progress

uv draws progress bars only when R runs in a terminal. In RStudio, Positron and
other IDE consoles, it prints one line when a large download starts and one
when it ends, with nothing in between, for example:

```
Downloading torch (846.0MiB)
 Downloaded torch
```

A large download can take several minutes. To see the progress, do the
first load in R running in a terminal. The download is cached, so your IDE
sessions use it afterwards.

### Intel Macs

On Intel Macs, TensorFlow can only be added before Python starts. If you load
a model that needs TensorFlow after Python has started (for example after
loading another model), birdnetR stops with:

```
On Intel Macs, TensorFlow must be added before Python starts. Restart R and make this load your first birdnetR call.
```

Restart R and load the TensorFlow model first. Perch v2 does not run on Intel
Macs at all.


## Your own Python environment

If you set `RETICULATE_PYTHON` to the Python of your own virtual environment,
birdnetR uses that environment and does not change it. This also means it
can't install the extras there. Install them yourself, for example with
`reticulate::virtualenv_install("my-env", "birdnet[tf]")` for TensorFlow or
`"birdnet[pt]"` for PyTorch. If a runtime is missing, the `birdnet` Python
package stops with an error that names it.

`RETICULATE_PYTHON` must be set before Python starts: in your `.Renviron` file,
or with `Sys.setenv()` before you load the first model.
`reticulate::use_virtualenv()` alone does not work with birdnetR, because
birdnetR sets `RETICULATE_PYTHON` to reticulate's managed environment when it
is unset, and `RETICULATE_PYTHON` takes precedence.

Some GPU setups need your own environment; see the [GPU](gpu.html) article.


## Working offline

Models are downloaded the first time you load them. Run your analysis once
while online, so that Python, the Python packages and the models are on disk.

When the environment variable `BIRDNET_OFFLINE` is `1`, the `birdnet` Python
package never tries to download anything. A model that is not on disk then
stops with an error that names its download URL. Set the variable before you
load a model:

```{r}
Sys.setenv(BIRDNET_OFFLINE = "1")
model <- birdnet_load()
```
